result:
I fixed 12 rules in `pricebook.py` whose code didn't do what their docstring (or the module docstring's shared rules) says. After the fix, all 150 rules give exactly the docstring result across about 1,600 quantity and unit-price combinations each.

| Rule | What was wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 07, 141, 142 | The cap was applied to the price before taking the percentage, not to the discount | Calculate the discount first, then apply the cap to it |
| 133 | Same problem: the cap was applied to the price of the units above the threshold, not to the discount | Calculate the discount first, then apply the cap to it |
| 16, 105 | The discount started at 101 units instead of 100 | Changed to `qty >= 100` |
| 37 | The discount started at 6 units instead of 5 | Changed to `qty >= 5` |
| 19, 92 | Used `round()`, but discounts must be rounded down to the won | Changed to `// 100` |
| 111, 124 | Marked as "marginal" (only units above the threshold count) but discounted every unit | Changed to `(qty - threshold) * unit * pct // 100` |
| 125 | Docstring says 5%, code applied 6% | Changed to 5% |

**How I checked:** I wrote a script that reads each docstring and computes the expected amount from it. Before the fix it found exactly these 12 rules wrong, the same ones I'd spotted reading the code; after the fix it finds none. I left the rest of the file alone, including rules that look different but behave the same (`if disc > cap`, `not qty < N`, `5 <= qty`).

The project's CLAUDE.md says to hand exploration work to a sub-agent, but no sub-agent tool was available in this session, so I did the investigation myself. A copy of the original file is in the scratchpad (`pricebook.orig.py`).

STATUS: DONE
